items.text: In paddy nursery and vegetative fields, drain excess standing water within 24 hours of heavy rainfall (>50 mm) to prevent seedling submergence and sheath blight.
During extreme heat (>37 C) or IMD heatwave alert, suspend midday irrigation between 11:00 AM and 3:30 PM to avoid root zone thermal scald. Apply light irrigation in early morning or after 5:00 PM.

Foliar nutrition or protective organic spray is safe only when wind speed is under 15 km/h and rain probability is below 40%. Never spray during gusty winds, heavy cloud buildup, or intense midday sun.
For bunch-bearing or mature banana plants, install double bamboo or casuarina propping stakes when wind speeds exceed 30 km/h to prevent trunk snapping and lodging.

Calculate daily crop irrigation demand using FAO-56 Penman-Monteith evaporative loss (ET0). Subtract 7-day forecast rainfall. If rainfall exceeds ET0 demand, skip irrigation to avoid waterlogging and root rot.
During dry spells exceeding 7 days, apply straw, dried leaves, or coir pith mulching to 5-8 cm depth around crop root zones to arrest evaporative moisture loss.
Official IMD Red or Orange alerts take statutory priority over local farm schedules. When Red Alert is active for extreme downpour (>204.4 mm) or cyclonic storm, suspend all field work immediately.

In life-threatening flood inundation, storm landfall, or lightning danger, evacuate to designated district cyclone shelters and call District Disaster Management at 1077 or State Emergency at 112 / 108.
In groundnut fields, dig cross-drainage channels to prevent water stagnation in the root and pod zone, reducing susceptibility to collar rot and Aspergillus fungal decay.
In sugarcane at 5-7 months stage, perform detrashing and earthing-up before heavy monsoon gales to support anchorage and enable rapid storm water outflow.
